[[竹田皇子]]墓 拝所}}]] '''山田高塚古墳'''（やまだたかつかこふん、高松古墳<たかまつこふん>{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}）は、[[大阪府]][[南河内郡]][[太子町 (大阪府)|太子町]]山田にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[方墳]]（または長方形墳）。[[磯長谷古墳群]]を構成する古墳の1つ。 実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[宮内庁]]により「'''磯長山田陵'''（しながのやまだのみささぎ）」および「'''竹田皇子墓'''（たけだのみこのはか）」として第33代[[推古天皇]]・[[竹田皇子]]（[[敏達天皇]][[皇子]]）の[[陵墓|合葬陵墓]]に治定されている。 == 概要 == 大阪府南東部、[[二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|二上山]]山麓の磯長谷において、金剛山地から伸びる台地状丘陵の西端部に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。[[江戸時代]]の修陵で大規模な改変が加えられているほか{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}、現在は[[宮内庁]]治定の天皇陵として同庁の管理下にあるが、これまでに[[宮内庁書陵部]]による調査等が実施されている{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。 墳丘は3段築成{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。1段目は正方形、3段目は長方形であるが、1段目形状には後世の改変可能性が指摘される{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。墳丘外表では貼石が認められるが、[[埴輪]]は無いとされる{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。埋葬施設は明らかでないが、東西に長い墳丘の特徴から、[[横穴式石室]]2基が東西に並び、いずれも南方に開口したと推定される{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。古書ではいずれかの石室内部における石棺2基の存在が記述されている{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。 被葬者は明らかでないが、現在は[[宮内庁]]により第33代[[推古天皇]]（[[628年]]崩御）および子の[[竹田皇子]]（崩御年不詳）の[[陵墓|合葬陵墓]]に治定されている{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。磯長谷では、長方形墳または双方墳の形式として[[二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|二子塚古墳]]（太子町山田）や[[葉室塚古墳]]（太子町葉室）が知られ、石室2基の点や墳丘比率の点で共通性が指摘される{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=33-41}}。また磯長谷では推古天皇陵のほか[[敏達天皇|敏達]]・[[用明天皇|用明]]・[[孝徳天皇]]陵と[[聖徳太子]]墓が伝わっており、これらは「梅鉢御陵」と総称される。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[康平]]3年（[[1060年]]）、「推古天皇山陵」で盗掘（『[[扶桑略記]]』『扶桑略記』康平3年（1060）6月2日条。）{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。 * [[1979年]]（[[昭和]]54年）、境界の石垣設置工事に伴う調査（[[宮内庁書陵部]]）{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。 * [[1989年]]度（[[平成]]元年度）、墳丘外表調査（宮内庁書陵部）{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。 * [[2012年]]（平成24年）2月23日、考古・歴史学会代表による立ち入り調査[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "推古天皇陵を立ち入り調査／研究者ら石室材を確認"]（四国新聞社、2012年2月23日記事）。。 == 構造 == [[File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|山田高塚古墳の航空写真
（1985年度）}}{{small|{{国土航空写真}}。}}]] 3段築成の墳丘のうち、1段目は東西59メートル・南北55メートルとほぼ正方形であるが、3段目は東西34メートル・南北25メートルと東西に長い長方形であり、かつ3段目は相当な急斜面をなす{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。墳丘全体の高さは11メートルを測る{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。特に1段目のプランは[[春日向山古墳]]（用明天皇陵）と同一になるため、江戸時代の修陵の際に春日向山古墳に則って改変されたと見られ、元は1段目も東西に長い長方形であった可能性が指摘される{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。 墳丘南側には前庭部状の平坦地があり、それを含めた陵域全体は東西75メートル・南北72メートルを測る{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。また墳丘東側・前面には空堀（幅8-9メートル）が認められるが、1979年（昭和54年）の調査によればその堤は後世に水田上に造作されたものとされる{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。 == 被葬者 == 山田高塚古墳の実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[宮内庁]]では第33代'''[[推古天皇]]'''および子の'''[[竹田皇子]]'''（たけだのみこ）の[[陵墓|合葬陵墓]]に治定している[https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/successive_list.html 天皇陵]（宮内庁）。宮内省諸陵寮編[{{NDLDC|1237123/12}} 『陵墓要覧』]（1934年、国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）11-12コマ。{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}『陵墓地形図集成 縮小版』 宮内庁書陵部陵墓課編、学生社、2014年、p. 407。。推古天皇について、『[[日本書紀]]』では推古天皇36年（[[628年]]）3月『日本書紀』推古天皇36年（628年）3月癸丑（7日）条。に崩御したとし、同年9月『日本書紀』推古天皇36年（628年）9月壬辰（24日）条。に遺詔により「竹田皇子之陵」に葬ったとするが、所在地・陵名に関する記載は無い{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。一方で『[[古事記]]』では、「御陵在大野岡上、後遷科長大陵也」として「大野岡上」から「科長大陵」への改葬の旨が見えるが、こちらには竹田皇子との合葬に関する記載は無い{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。『[[延喜式]]』[[諸陵式|諸陵寮]]『延喜式』巻21（治部省）諸陵寮条。では、推古天皇陵は遠陵の「磯長山田陵」として記載され、[[河内国]][[石川郡 (大阪府)|石川郡]]の所在で、兆域は東西2町・南北2町で陵戸1烟・守戸4烟を毎年あてるとする{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。また『[[扶桑略記]]』によれば、[[康平]]3年（[[1060年]]）に「推古天皇山陵」で盗掘があったという{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。 その後、[[元禄]]の探陵の際には堺奉行が現陵の存在を報告している{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。また古書では、横穴式石室（いずれの石室か不明）の内部には石棺2基があって、右が推古天皇棺で左が竹田皇子棺であると見える{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=33-41}}。ただし前述のように本古墳には2基の石室の存在が推定されるため、性格を規定するには石棺2基の石室とは別の石室の内容も考慮するべき点が注意される{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。 [[File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|山田高塚古墳から望む
[[二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|二子塚古墳]]}}]] なお、推古天皇・竹田皇子の真の合葬陵墓としては東方約200メートルの[[二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|二子塚古墳]]に比定する説もあるほか{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=33-41}}、改葬前の陵墓（大野岡上）については[[植山古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[橿原市]]）に比定する説がある（詳細は「[[植山古墳]]」参照）。 {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 auto;white-space:nowrap;background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+梅鉢御陵関係系図 |- |{{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0||||01|~|y|~|~|~|~|~|~|~|~|~|~|02|~|y|~|03| 01=[[石姫皇女|{{color|#FC4E6B|'''石姫'''}}]]

[[竹田皇子]]墓 拝所}}]] '''山田高塚古墳'''（やまだたかつかこふん）は、[[大阪府]][[南河内郡]][[太子町 (大阪府)|太子町]]山田にある[[古墳]]。'''高松古墳'''（たかまつこふん）{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}ともいう。形状は[[方墳]]（または長方形墳）。[[磯長谷古墳群]]を構成する古墳の1つ。 実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[宮内庁]]により「'''磯長山田陵'''（しながのやまだのみささぎ）」および「'''竹田皇子墓'''（たけだのみこのはか）」として第33代[[推古天皇]]・[[竹田皇子]]（[[敏達天皇]][[皇子]]）の[[陵墓|合葬陵墓]]に治定されている。 == 概要 == 大阪府南東部、[[二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|二上山]]山麓の磯長谷において、金剛山地から伸びる台地状丘陵の西端部に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。[[江戸時代]]の修陵で大規模な改変が加えられているほか{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}、現在は[[宮内庁]]治定の天皇陵として同庁の管理下にあるが、これまでに[[宮内庁書陵部]]による調査等が実施されている{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。 墳丘は3段築成{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。1段目は正方形、3段目は長方形であるが、1段目形状には後世の改変可能性が指摘される{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。墳丘外表では貼石が認められるが、[[埴輪]]は無いとされる{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。埋葬施設は明らかでないが、東西に長い墳丘の特徴から、[[横穴式石室]]2基が東西に並び、いずれも南方に開口したと推定される{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。古書ではいずれかの石室内部における石棺2基の存在が記述されている{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。 被葬者は明らかでないが、現在は[[宮内庁]]により第33代[[推古天皇]]（[[628年]]崩御）および子の[[竹田皇子]]（崩御年不詳）の[[陵墓|合葬陵墓]]に治定されている{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。磯長谷では、長方形墳または双方墳の形式として[[二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|二子塚古墳]]（太子町山田）や[[葉室塚古墳]]（太子町葉室）が知られ、石室2基の点や墳丘比率の点で共通性が指摘される{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=33-41}}。また磯長谷では推古天皇陵のほか[[敏達天皇|敏達]]・[[用明天皇|用明]]・[[孝徳天皇]]陵と[[聖徳太子]]墓が伝わっており、これらは「梅鉢御陵」と総称される。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[康平]]3年（[[1060年]]）、「推古天皇山陵」で盗掘（『[[扶桑略記]]』『扶桑略記』康平3年（1060）6月2日条。）{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。 * [[1979年]]（[[昭和]]54年）、境界の石垣設置工事に伴う調査（[[宮内庁書陵部]]）{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。 * [[1989年]]度（[[平成]]元年度）、墳丘外表調査（宮内庁書陵部）{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。 * [[2012年]]（平成24年）2月23日、考古・歴史学会代表による立ち入り調査[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "推古天皇陵を立ち入り調査／研究者ら石室材を確認"]（四国新聞社、2012年2月23日記事）。。 == 構造 == [[File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|山田高塚古墳の航空写真
（1985年度）}}{{small|{{国土航空写真}}。}}]] 3段築成の墳丘のうち、1段目は東西59メートル・南北55メートルとほぼ正方形であるが、3段目は東西34メートル・南北25メートルと東西に長い長方形であり、かつ3段目は相当な急斜面をなす{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。墳丘全体の高さは11メートルを測る{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。特に1段目のプランは[[春日向山古墳]]（用明天皇陵）と同一になるため、江戸時代の修陵の際に春日向山古墳に則って改変されたと見られ、元は1段目も東西に長い長方形であった可能性が指摘される{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。 墳丘南側には前庭部状の平坦地があり、それを含めた陵域全体は東西75メートル・南北72メートルを測る{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。また墳丘東側・前面には空堀（幅8-9メートル）が認められるが、1979年（昭和54年）の調査によればその堤は後世に水田上に造作されたものとされる{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。 == 被葬者 == 山田高塚古墳の実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[宮内庁]]では第33代'''[[推古天皇]]'''および子の'''[[竹田皇子]]'''（たけだのみこ）の[[陵墓|合葬陵墓]]に治定している[https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/successive_list.html 天皇陵]（宮内庁）。宮内省諸陵寮編[{{NDLDC|1237123/12}} 『陵墓要覧』]（1934年、国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）11-12コマ。{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}『陵墓地形図集成 縮小版』 宮内庁書陵部陵墓課編、学生社、2014年、p. 407。。推古天皇について、『[[日本書紀]]』では推古天皇36年（[[628年]]）3月『日本書紀』推古天皇36年（628年）3月癸丑（7日）条。に崩御したとし、同年9月『日本書紀』推古天皇36年（628年）9月壬辰（24日）条。に遺詔により「竹田皇子之陵」に葬ったとするが、所在地・陵名に関する記載は無い{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}。一方で『[[古事記]]』では、「御陵在大野岡上、後遷科長大陵也」として「大野岡上」から「科長大陵」への改葬の旨が見えるが、こちらには竹田皇子との合葬に関する記載は無い{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。『[[延喜式]]』[[諸陵式|諸陵寮]]『延喜式』巻21（治部省）諸陵寮条。では、推古天皇陵は遠陵の「磯長山田陵」として記載され、[[河内国]][[石川郡 (大阪府)|石川郡]]の所在で、兆域は東西2町・南北2町で陵戸1烟・守戸4烟を毎年あてるとする{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。また『[[扶桑略記]]』によれば、[[康平]]3年（[[1060年]]）に「推古天皇山陵」で盗掘があったという{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。 その後、[[元禄]]の探陵の際には堺奉行が現陵の存在を報告している{{Sfn|磯長山田陵（国史）}}。また古書では、横穴式石室（いずれの石室か不明）の内部には石棺2基があって、右が推古天皇棺で左が竹田皇子棺であると見える{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=33-41}}。ただし前述のように本古墳には2基の石室の存在が推定されるため、性格を規定するには石棺2基の石室とは別の石室の内容も考慮するべき点が注意される{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}。 [[File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|山田高塚古墳から望む
[[二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|二子塚古墳]]}}]] なお、推古天皇・竹田皇子の真の合葬陵墓としては東方約200メートルの[[二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|二子塚古墳]]に比定する説もあるほか{{Sfn|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=33-41}}、改葬前の陵墓（大野岡上）については[[植山古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[橿原市]]）に比定する説がある（詳細は「[[植山古墳]]」参照）。 {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 auto;white-space:nowrap;background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+梅鉢御陵関係系図 |- |{{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0||||01|~|y|~|~|~|~|~|~|~|~|~|~|02|~|y|~|03| 01=[[石姫皇女|{{color|#FC4E6B|'''石姫'''}}]]

revision.text:
{{draft}} [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|thumb]] {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{draft categories|[[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{draft categories| [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Kk]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:draft:{{PAGENAME}}]] }} ==Overview== [[category:new pages]] {{Infobox Japanese Kofun | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the tumulus | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | group = {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}} | latitude = 34.511896 | longitude = 135.649556 | ISO = JP-27 | shape = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳}} (or rectangular tumulus) | dimensions = East-west: 59m × North-south: 55m
Height: 11m | construction_period = | burial_facility = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室}} | buried_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and [[Prince Takeda]] | artifacts = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijo|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kongo Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''Location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} * Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) * Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}) * Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) * Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]

Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{draft categories|[[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{draft categories| [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Kk]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:draft:{{PAGENAME}}]] }} ==Overview== [[category:new pages]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]

Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijo|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kongo Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} * Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) * Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}) * Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) * Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]

The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. AD), however [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{draft categories| [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Kk]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:draft:{{PAGENAME}}]] }} ==Overview== [[Category:Pages with redlinks to fill]] [[Category:kkk]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[category:kk]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]

Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijo|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kongo Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} * Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) * Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}) * Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) * Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:kk]][[category:kk]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]

Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{draft categories|[[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{draft categories| [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Kk]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:draft:{{PAGENAME}} }} ==Overview== [[Category:Pages with redlinks to fill]] [[Category:kkk]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[category:kk]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the tumulus | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | group = {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}} | latitude = 34.511896 | longitude = 135.649556 | ISO = JP-27 | shape = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳}} (or rectangular tumulus) | dimensions = East-west: 59m × North-south: 55m
Height: 11m | construction_period = | burial_facility = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室}} | buried_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and [[Prince Takeda]] | artifacts = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijo|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kongo Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:kk]][[category:kk]] [[Category:attempting to force efresh]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]

Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijo|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kongo Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Kk]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== [[Category:Pages with redlinks to fill]] [[Category:kkk]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[category:kk]] '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijo|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:kk]][[category:kk]] [[Category:attempting to force efresh]] [[Category:attempting to force refresh]] [[Category:mass editing for the third subcategory]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]

Height: 11m | construction_period = | burial_facility = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室}} | buried_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and [[Prince Takeda]] | artifacts = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Kk]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== [[Category:Pages with redlinks to fill]][[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[category:kk]] '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:kk]][[category:kk]] [[Category:attempting to force efresh]] [[Category:attempting to force refresh]] [[Category:mass editing for the third subcategory]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]

Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ''' Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ''' Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ''' Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ''' Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:kk]][[category:kk]] [[Category:attempting to force efresh]] [[Category:attempting to force refresh]] [[Category:mass editing for the third subcategory]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]

Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Kk]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== [[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[category:kk]] '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:kk]][[category:kk]] [[Category:attempting to force efresh]] [[Category:attempting to force refresh]] [[Category:mass editing for the third subcategory]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]

'''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:kk]][[category:kk]] [[Category:attempting to force efresh]] [[Category:attempting to force refresh]] [[Category:mass editing for the third subcategory]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]

Height: 11m | construction_period = | burial_facility = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室}} | buried_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and [[Prince Takeda]] | artifacts = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Kk]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== [[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[category:kk]] '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:kk]][[category:kk]] [[Category:attempting to force efresh]] [[Category:attempting to force refresh]] [[Category:mass editing for the third subcategory]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:mass bump]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]]
