(''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] Tumulus}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] Tumulus}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] Tumulus}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] Tumulus}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Tumulus]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) == References == '''Primary Sources''' Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]]
