Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Default sort converted to citation needed]] {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) ==Merge== needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | Alternate name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} | Latitude = 34.5119 | Longitude = 135.6496 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | Dimensions = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | Burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | Interred individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda | Excavated items = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | Map = Japan Osaka | Label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | Icon = Square tumulus | Label position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628年}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == Notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} * {{draft}} {{afc comment|1=although this one comes from a wikipedia draft, it is actually not from everybodywiki. I got the history properly imported[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:46, 13 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the tumulus | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | group = {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}} | latitude = 34.511896 | longitude = 135.649556 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | dimensions = East-west: 59m × North-south: 55m
Height: 11m | construction_period = | burial_facility = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | buried_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and [[Prince Takeda]] | artifacts = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) ==Merge== View of the entire mound | Alternate name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} | Latitude = 34.5119 | Longitude = 135.6496 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | Dimensions = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | Burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | Interred individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda | Excavated items = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | Map = Japan Osaka | Label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | Icon = Square tumulus | Label position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628年}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka I got the history properly imported[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:46, 13 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the tumulus | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | group = {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}} | latitude = 34.511896 | longitude = 135.649556 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | dimensions = East-west: 59m × North-south: 55m
Height: 11m | construction_period = | burial_facility = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | buried_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and [[Prince Takeda]] | artifacts = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Default sort converted to citation needed]] {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Default sort converted to citation needed]] {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) ==Merge== needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | Alternate name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} | Latitude = 34.5119 | Longitude = 135.6496 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | Dimensions = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | Burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | Interred individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda | Excavated items = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | Map = Japan Osaka | Label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | Icon = Square tumulus | Label position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628年}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Full view of the tumulus | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | group = {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}} | latitude = 34.511896 | longitude = 135.649556 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | dimensions = East-west: 59m × North-south: 55m
Height: 11m | construction_period = | burial_facility = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | buried_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and [[Prince Takeda]] | artifacts = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Default sort converted to citation needed]] {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) ==Merge== needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | Alternate name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} | Latitude = 34.5119 | Longitude = 135.6496 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | Dimensions = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | Burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | Interred individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda | Excavated items = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | Map = Japan Osaka | Label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | Icon = Square tumulus | Label position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628年}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} kofun. Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | Burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | Interred individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda | Excavated items = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | Map = Japan Osaka | Label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | Icon = Square tumulus | Label position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628年}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka I got the history properly imported[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:46, 13 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the tumulus | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | group = {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}} | latitude = 34.511896 | longitude = 135.649556 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | dimensions = East-west: 59m × North-south: 55m
Height: 11m | construction_period = | burial_facility = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | buried_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and [[Prince Takeda]] | artifacts = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Default sort converted to citation needed]] {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Default sort converted to citation needed]] {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) ==Merge== View of the entire mound | Alternate name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} | Latitude = 34.5119 | Longitude = 135.6496 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | Dimensions = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | Burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | Interred individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda | Excavated items = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | Map = Japan Osaka | Label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | Icon = Square tumulus | Label position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628年}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka I got the history properly imported[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:46, 13 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the tumulus | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | group = {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}} | latitude = 34.511896 | longitude = 135.649556 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | dimensions = East-west: 59m × North-south: 55m
Height: 11m | construction_period = | burial_facility = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | buried_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and [[Prince Takeda]] | artifacts = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | icon = Square tumulus | label_position = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} kofun. [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories|[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Default sort converted to citation needed]] {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Default sort converted to citation needed]] {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]]{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} and is designated as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original shape of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == Structure == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, forming a nearly square shape. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, forming a rectangular shape with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳}}) ==Merge== needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}[[ja:山田高塚古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | Alternate name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} | Latitude = 34.5119 | Longitude = 135.6496 | ISO = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) | Dimensions = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | Burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | Interred individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda | Excavated items = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | Map = Japan Osaka | Label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | Icon = Square tumulus | Label position = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Burial Mounds|ja|磯長谷古墳群}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628年}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka
