Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=draft}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|12=draft}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=draft}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories| }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|12=draft}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|12=draft}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線|12=draft}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=draft}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|12=draft}}) ==Merge== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|12=draft}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|12=draft}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628th year|12=draft}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town Homepage {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線|12=draft}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=draft}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|12=draft}}) ==Merge== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|12=draft}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|12=draft}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628th year|12=draft}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town Homepage {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * {{ill|Ueyama Kofun|ja|植山古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|12=draft}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628th year|12=draft}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=draft}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|12=draft}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=draft}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories| }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|12=draft}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|12=draft}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線|12=draft}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=draft}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628th year|12=draft}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=draft}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|12=draft}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=draft}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories| }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|12=draft}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|12=draft}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線|12=draft}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=draft}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=draft}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|12=draft}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=draft}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} {{draft categories| }}There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|12=draft}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|12=draft}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線|12=draft}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=draft}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|12=draft}}) ==Merge== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|12=draft}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|12=draft}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628th year|12=draft}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town Homepage {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka AD), however {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] ==Overview== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}{{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}'''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}, {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|12=draft}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|12=draft}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線|12=draft}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=draft}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|12=draft}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628th year|12=draft}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasugayama Kofun|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線|12=draft}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=draft}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|12=draft}}) ==Merge== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|12=draft}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinga Valley Kofuns|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Isonokami Valley Kofun Group|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|12=draft}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628th year|12=draft}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|ja|二子塚古墳 (大阪府太子町)|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=draft}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町 (大阪府)|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|ja|喜志駅|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Nagano Line|ja|近鉄長野線|12=draft}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=draft}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=draft}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|12=draft}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|12=draft}}) ==Merge== {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{citation needed|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|12=draft}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=draft}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}} | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | Construction year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District|ja|南河内郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|12=draft}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Mountain Range|ja|金剛山地|12=draft}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|12=draft}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Shoryobu Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部|1=Archives and Mausolea Department|12=draft}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|12=draft}} (deceased {{ill|628|ja|628th year|12=draft}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun
