Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|qq=}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however ==Overview== '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of [[:en:Mount Nijō|Mount Nijō]] in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]].{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]] and {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasugayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From [[:en:Kishi Station (Osaka)|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)]] ([[:en:Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|Kintetsu Nagano Line]]), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kongō Bus|qq=}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ([[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]]) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifukuji North Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}) ==Merge== {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|qq=}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | built year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individual = ([[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site) [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda (the son of [[:en:Emperor Bidatsu|Emperor Bidatsu]]). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kongō Mountain Range]] in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|1=Futakami Mountain|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}. Significant modifications were made during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], with archaeological investigations conducted by its [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Archives and Mausolea Department]]{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] designates it as the joint mausoleum of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] (deceased [[:en:628|628]]) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in [[:en:Kawachi Province|Kawachi Province]], with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town Homepage == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * [[:en:Ueyama Kofun|Ueyama Kofun]] * [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]], {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|山田高塚古墳|version=100823654|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Shinagadani Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Ancient Kofuns in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Archives and Mausolea Department]] [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[sn:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[sn:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]]}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[sn:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[sn:amada Takazuka Kofun]] [[sn:amada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:大阪府太子町の歴史]] [[Category:推古天皇]] [[Category:磯長谷古墳群]]

Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|qq=}}. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however ==Overview== '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of [[:en:Mount Nijō|Mount Nijō]] in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]].{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]] and {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasugayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From [[:en:Kishi Station (Osaka)|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)]] ([[:en:Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|Kintetsu Nagano Line]]), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kongō Bus|qq=}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ([[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]]) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifukuji North Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}) ==Merge== {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|qq=}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | built year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individual = ([[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site) [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda (the son of [[:en:Emperor Bidatsu|Emperor Bidatsu]]). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kongō Mountain Range]] in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|1=Futakami Mountain|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}. Significant modifications were made during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], with archaeological investigations conducted by its [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Archives and Mausolea Department]]{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] designates it as the joint mausoleum of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] (deceased [[:en:628|628]]) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in [[:en:Kawachi Province|Kawachi Province]], with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town Homepage == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * [[:en:Ueyama Kofun|Ueyama Kofun]] * [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]], {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - AD), however ==Overview== '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of [[:en:Mount Nijō|Mount Nijō]] in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]].{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]] and {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasugayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From [[:en:Kishi Station (Osaka)|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)]] ([[:en:Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|Kintetsu Nagano Line]]), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kongō Bus|qq=}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ([[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]]) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifukuji North Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}) ==Merge== {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|qq=}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | built year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individual = ([[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site) [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda (the son of [[:en:Emperor Bidatsu|Emperor Bidatsu]]). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kongō Mountain Range]] in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|1=Futakami Mountain|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}. Significant modifications were made during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], with archaeological investigations conducted by its [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Archives and Mausolea Department]]{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] designates it as the joint mausoleum of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] (deceased [[:en:628|628]]) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in [[:en:Kawachi Province|Kawachi Province]], with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town Homepage == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * [[:en:Ueyama Kofun|Ueyama Kofun]] * [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]], {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|山田高塚古墳|version=100823654|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Shinagadani Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Ancient Kofuns in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Archives and Mausolea Department]] [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[sn:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[sn:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]]}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[sn:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[sn:amada Takazuka Kofun]] [[sn:amada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:大阪府太子町の歴史]] [[Category:推古天皇]] [[Category:磯長谷古墳群]] [[Category:長方形墳]]

The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however ==Overview== '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of [[:en:Mount Nijō|Mount Nijō]] in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]].{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]] and {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasugayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From [[:en:Kishi Station (Osaka)|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)]] ([[:en:Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|Kintetsu Nagano Line]]), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kongō Bus|qq=}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ([[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]]) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifukuji North Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}) ==Merge== {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|qq=}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | built year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individual = ([[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site) [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda (the son of [[:en:Emperor Bidatsu|Emperor Bidatsu]]). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kongō Mountain Range]] in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|1=Futakami Mountain|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}. Significant modifications were made during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], with archaeological investigations conducted by its [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Archives and Mausolea Department]]{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] designates it as the joint mausoleum of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] (deceased [[:en:628|628]]) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in [[:en:Kawachi Province|Kawachi Province]], with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town Homepage == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * [[:en:Ueyama Kofun|Ueyama Kofun]] * [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]], {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] - Imperial Household Agency * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town website {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|山田高塚古墳|version=100823654|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Rectangular Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:Square Kofun]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Shinagadani Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Ancient Kofuns in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Imperial tombs of Japan]] [[Category:Empress Suiko]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Archives and Mausolea Department]] [[Category:Isonokami Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Taishi, Osaka]] [[Category:burial sites of Japanese emperors]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[sn:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]][[sn:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]]}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[sn:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[ja:山田高塚古墳]] [[en:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[sn:amada Takazuka Kofun]] [[sn:amada Takatsuka Kofun]] [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:大阪府太子町の歴史]] [[Category:推古天皇]] [[Category:磯長谷古墳群]] [[Category:長方形墳]] {{Commons category|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}}

Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|qq=}}. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} There is a tradition that the [[Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun]] is the true tomb of the 33rd [[Empress Suiko]] (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however ==Overview== '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of [[Empress Suiko]] (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]].{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of [[:en:Mount Nijō|Mount Nijō]] in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]].{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] as a shared mausoleum for [[Empress Suiko]] (d. 628 CE) and her son, [[Prince Takeda]] (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]] and {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasugayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * [[:en:Taishi, Osaka|Taishi, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From [[:en:Kishi Station (Osaka)|Kishi Station (Kintetsu)]] ([[:en:Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|Kintetsu Nagano Line]]), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kongō Bus|qq=}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ([[:en:Kongō Range|Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun]]) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifukuji North Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}) ==Merge== {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|qq=}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | built year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individual = ([[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site) [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|qq=}}, [[:en:Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Minamikawachi District]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] and Prince Takeda (the son of [[:en:Emperor Bidatsu|Emperor Bidatsu]]). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the [[:en:Kongō Range|Kongō Mountain Range]] in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|1=Futakami Mountain|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}. Significant modifications were made during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]], with archaeological investigations conducted by its [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Archives and Mausolea Department]]{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two stone coffins inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] designates it as the joint mausoleum of [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] (deceased [[:en:628|628]]) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in [[:en:Kawachi Province|Kawachi Province]], with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Taishi Town Homepage == References == '''Primary Sources''' {{reflist|group="primary"}} '''Secondary Sources''' {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[Empress Suiko]] * [[Prince Takeda]] * [[:en:Ueyama Kofun|Ueyama Kofun]] * [[:en:Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)]], {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun}} * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Official page for Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum] -
