Height: 11m | built = | burial = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoana-style stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}}) {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (33rd emperor of Japan) and {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi}} | burial goods = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11470748}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Takeda Tomb|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top | architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353}} | commemorates = {{ill|Prince Takeda|WD=Q11599359}}; {{ill|Suiko|WD=Q298057}} }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} There is a tradition that the {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|en|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|WD=Q11371443|lt=Futagozuka Kofun}} is the true tomb of the 33rd {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however ==Overview== '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|en|Taishi, Osaka|WD=Q1347173|lt=Taishi, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi}}.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|en|Mount Nijō|WD=Q11371271|lt=Mount Nijō}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} as a shared mausoleum for {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (d. 628 CE) and her son, {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi}} (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|en|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|WD=Q11371443|lt=Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)}} and {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=葉室古墳群}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasugayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|en|Taishi, Osaka|WD=Q1347173|lt=Taishi, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Osaka)|en|Kishi Station (Osaka)|WD=Q6416576|lt=Kishi Station (Kintetsu)}} ({{ill|Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|en|Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|WD=Q901413|lt=Kintetsu Nagano Line}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kongō Bus|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=金剛自動車|1=Kongo Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11646543}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifukuji North Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}) ==Merge== {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10856365}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|en|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|WD=Q1347323|lt=Minamikawachi District}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}} | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | built year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10856365}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|en|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|WD=Q1347323|lt=Minamikawachi District}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|en|Emperor Bidatsu|WD=Q316637|lt=Emperor Bidatsu}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kongō Mountain Range}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|1=Futakami Mountain|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two Sarcophaguss inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (deceased {{ill|628|en|628|WD=Q30592|lt=628}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|WD=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Height: 11m | built = | burial = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoana-style stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}}) {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (33rd emperor of Japan) and {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi}} | burial goods = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11470748}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Takeda Tomb|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top | architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353}} | commemorates = {{ill|Prince Takeda|WD=Q11599359}}; {{ill|Suiko|WD=Q298057}} }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} There is a tradition that the {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|en|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|WD=Q11371443|lt=Futagozuka Kofun}} is the true tomb of the 33rd {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however ==Overview== '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|en|Taishi, Osaka|WD=Q1347173|lt=Taishi, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi}}.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|en|Mount Nijō|WD=Q11371271|lt=Mount Nijō}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} as a shared mausoleum for {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (d. 628 CE) and her son, {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi}} (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|en|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|WD=Q11371443|lt=Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)}} and {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=葉室古墳群}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasugayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|en|Taishi, Osaka|WD=Q1347173|lt=Taishi, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Osaka)|en|Kishi Station (Osaka)|WD=Q6416576|lt=Kishi Station (Kintetsu)}} ({{ill|Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|en|Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|WD=Q901413|lt=Kintetsu Nagano Line}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kongō Bus|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=金剛自動車|1=Kongo Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11646543}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifukuji North Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}) ==Merge== {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10856365}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|en|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|WD=Q1347323|lt=Minamikawachi District}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}} | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | built year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10856365}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|en|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|WD=Q1347323|lt=Minamikawachi District}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|en|Emperor Bidatsu|WD=Q316637|lt=Emperor Bidatsu}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kongō Mountain Range}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|1=Futakami Mountain|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two Sarcophaguss inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko}} (deceased {{ill|628|en|628|WD=Q30592|lt=628}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|WD=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Height: 11m | built = | burial = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoana-style stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}}) {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (33rd emperor of Japan) and {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi|1=Prince Takechi}} | burial goods = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11470748}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Takeda Tomb|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top | architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353|1=Square Kofun}} | commemorates = {{ill|Prince Takeda|WD=Q11599359|1=Prince Takeda}}; {{ill|Suiko|WD=Q298057|1=Empress Suiko}} }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} There is a tradition that the {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|en|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|WD=Q11371443|lt=Futagozuka Kofun|1=Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)}} is the true tomb of the 33rd {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however ==Overview== '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|en|Taishi, Osaka|WD=Q1347173|lt=Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishi, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi|1=Prince Takechi}}.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|en|Mount Nijō|WD=Q11371271|lt=Mount Nijō|1=Mount Nijō}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|1=Kongō Range}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} as a shared mausoleum for {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (d. 628 CE) and her son, {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi|1=Prince Takechi}} (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|en|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|WD=Q11371443|lt=Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|1=Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)}} and {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=葉室古墳群}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasugayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|en|Taishi, Osaka|WD=Q1347173|lt=Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishi, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Osaka)|en|Kishi Station (Osaka)|WD=Q6416576|lt=Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|1=Kishi Station (Osaka)}} ({{ill|Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|en|Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|WD=Q901413|lt=Kintetsu Nagano Line|1=Nagano Line (Kintetsu)}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kongō Bus|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=金剛自動車|1=Kongo Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11646543}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|1=Kongō Range}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifukuji North Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}) ==Merge== {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]

Height: 11m | built year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10856365}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|en|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|WD=Q1347323|lt=Minamikawachi District|1=Minamikawachi District, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|en|Emperor Bidatsu|WD=Q316637|lt=Emperor Bidatsu|1=Emperor Bidatsu}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kongō Mountain Range|1=Kongō Range}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|1=Futakami Mountain|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two Sarcophaguss inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (deceased {{ill|628|en|628|WD=Q30592|lt=628|1=628}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|WD=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province|1=Kawachi Province}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] - {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} * [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/kanko_info/rekishi_shiseki/suikotennoryo.html Empress Suiko Mausoleum] - Height: 11m | built = | burial = (Presumed) Two {{ill|yokoana-style stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoana-style stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individuals = (Designated by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}}) {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (33rd emperor of Japan) and {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi|1=Prince Takechi}} | burial goods = | mausoleum = Designated as {{ill|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja|磯長山田陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11470748}} and {{ill|Prince Takeda Tomb|ja|竹田皇子墓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Takeda Tomb|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | noteworthy = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka
Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top | architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353|1=Square Kofun}} | commemorates = {{ill|Prince Takeda|WD=Q11599359|1=Prince Takeda}}; {{ill|Suiko|WD=Q298057|1=Empress Suiko}} }} {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}} is a [[Kofun]] in Japan. Specifically, it is a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|1=Rectangular Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. It may alternatively be a {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} kofun. The Imperial Household Agency has proclaimed the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|1=Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}}'''|山田高塚古墳||}} 200 meters to the west to be her official grave site.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}} There is a tradition that the {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|en|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|WD=Q11371443|lt=Futagozuka Kofun|1=Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)}} is the true tomb of the 33rd {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (died 628 AD) and her son Prince Takeda (died 593? AD), however ==Overview== '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|en|Taishi, Osaka|WD=Q1347173|lt=Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishi, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}. It is also known as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳).{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and is Historic Site1 as a square tumulus (or rectangular-shaped tumulus). Although the actual individuals interred are unclear, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} has Historic Site1 it as the mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (33rd emperor of Japan) and her son, {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi|1=Prince Takechi}}.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} == Overview == Located in the southeastern part of Osaka Prefecture, near the foothills of {{ill|Mount Nijō|en|Mount Nijō|WD=Q11371271|lt=Mount Nijō|1=Mount Nijō}} in the Isonokami Valley, Yamada Takatsuka Kofun is built on a plateau at the western edge of the {{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|1=Kongō Range}}.{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} Significant modifications were made during the Edo period{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}}. The kofun is currently under the management of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}}, which has conducted several surveys.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The tumulus has a three-tiered structure.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} While the first tier is square and the third tier is rectangular, the original type of the first tier may have been modified in later periods.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} Stone cladding was used on the mound's surface, though no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} remains have been discovered.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The burial facility likely consisted of two horizontally aligned stone chambers, each opening to the south.{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} The burial site is currently Historic Site1 by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} as a shared mausoleum for {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (d. 628 CE) and her son, {{ill|Prince Takechi|en|Prince Takechi|WD=Q837590|lt=Prince Takechi|1=Prince Takechi}} (date of death unknown).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} Similar kofun, such as {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|en|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|WD=Q11371443|lt=Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|1=Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)}} and {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=葉室古墳群}}, suggest comparable designs.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=33-41}} == Historical Timeline == * 1060 CE: The mausoleum was looted. (''Fusō Ryakki'')''Fusō Ryakki'', entry for June 2, 1060.{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1979: Survey conducted during stone boundary installation (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Isonokami Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|}} * 1989: External examination of the tumulus (Imperial Household Agency).{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|1991}} * 2012: Archaeological access granted to researchers.[https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/culture_entertainment/20120223000513 "Researchers confirm stone chamber materials at Suiko Mausoleum"] (Shikoku Shimbun, February 23, 2012). == burial == The tumulus is three-tiered, with the base measuring 59 meters east-west and 55 meters north-south, typeing a nearly square type. The third tier measures 34 meters east-west and 25 meters north-south, typeing a rectangular type with steep slopes.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} The overall height of the mound is 11 meters.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} It has been suggested that the first tier was originally rectangular but was altered during the Edo period to match the layout of the nearby {{ill|Kasugayama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|1=Kasugayama Kofun|1=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|2=ja|3=春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasugayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Valley of Royal Tombs|1994|pp=16-17}} == Access == '''location''' * {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|en|Taishi, Osaka|WD=Q1347173|lt=Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishi, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}} '''Public Transport''' * Bus: From {{ill|Kishi Station (Osaka)|en|Kishi Station (Osaka)|WD=Q6416576|lt=Kishi Station (Kintetsu)|1=Kishi Station (Osaka)}} ({{ill|Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|en|Nagano Line (Kintetsu)|WD=Q901413|lt=Kintetsu Nagano Line|1=Nagano Line (Kintetsu)}}), take {{ill|Kongō Bus|ja|金剛バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kongō Bus|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=金剛自動車|1=Kongo Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11646543}} to "Goryomae" bus stop, then walk approximately 200 meters. '''Surrounding Sites''' * {{ill|Isonokami Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} ** Emperor Bidatsu's and Empress Ishihime's Tombs ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|1=Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Yōmei's Tomb ({{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun|1=Kongō Range}}) ** Prince Shōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Eifukuji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|1=Eifuku-ji North Kofun|2=ja|3=叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifukuji North Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}) ** Emperor Kōtoku's Tomb ({{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}) ==Merge== {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | name = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | image = [[File:Yamada Takatsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
View of the entire mound | alternate_name = Takamatsu Kofun | Cluster = {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}} | location = {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10856365}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|en|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|WD=Q1347323|lt=Minamikawachi District|1=Minamikawachi District, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}} | coordinates = 34.5119 | coordinates = 135.6496 | omitted = JP-27 | type = {{ill|Square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (or rectangular tumulus) | area = 59m (east-west) × 55m (north-south)
Height: 11m | built year = Unknown | burial chamber = (Assumed) Two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} | Interred_individual = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site) {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} and Prince Takeda | excavations = | Imperial tomb = {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site: "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum" and "Prince Takeda's Tomb" | Features = | map = Japan Osaka | map_dot_label = Yamada Takatsuka Kofun | type = Square tumulus | map_dot_label = top }} '''Yamada Takatsuka Kofun''' (山田高塚古墳) is an ancient {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|ja|太子町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi, Osaka|1=Taishichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10856365}}, {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|en|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|WD=Q1347323|lt=Minamikawachi District|1=Minamikawachi District, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}. Also referred to as '''Takamatsu Kofun''' (高松古墳){{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. It is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (or rectangular tumulus) and part of the {{ill|Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|ja|磯長谷古墳群|1=Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinagadani Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Shinga Yamada Mausoleum'''" (磯長山田陵) and "'''Prince Takeda's Tomb'''" (竹田皇子墓), the joint tomb of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} and Prince Takeda (the son of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|en|Emperor Bidatsu|WD=Q316637|lt=Emperor Bidatsu|1=Emperor Bidatsu}}). == Overview == The mound is located in southeastern Osaka Prefecture at the western edge of a plateau extending from the {{ill|Kongō Range|en|Kongō Range|WD=Q11646528|lt=Kongō Mountain Range|1=Kongō Range}} in the Shinga Valley near {{ill|Mount Nijō|ja|二上山|1=Futakami Mountain|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}. Significant modifications were made during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}} restoration{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}, and the site is now managed as an imperial tomb under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}}, with archaeological investigations conducted by its {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}}{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. The tumulus is built in three stages{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The first stage is square, while the third is rectangular, although post-construction modifications to the first stage are suggested{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. Surface paving stones are observed on the mound, but no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} have been found{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. The burial chamber is unknown, but the elongated mound suggests two {{ill|horizontal stone chambers|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chambers|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} arranged east to west, both opening southward{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}. Historical records mention the presence of two Sarcophaguss inside one of the chambers{{Sfn|Shoryobu Bulletin No. 42|ja|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991}}{{Sfn|Shinga Valley Tombs|ja|王陵の谷・磯長谷古墳群|1994|pp=16-17}}. == Interred Individuals == The exact individuals interred at Yamada Takatsuka Kofun are unknown. However, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the joint mausoleum of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|WD=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}} (deceased {{ill|628|en|628|WD=Q30592|lt=628|1=628}}) and her son, Prince Takeda (year of death unknown){{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}, Empress Suiko passed away in the 36th year of her reign (March 628)Nihon Shoki, Suiko 36th Year (628), March 7 (Kinoto no Ushi)., and was interred in "Prince Takeda's Tomb" per her final testament. The location and name of the tomb are not specified{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}} describes it as the "Shinga Yamada Mausoleum," a "distant tomb" in {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|WD=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province|1=Kawachi Province}}, with a precinct spanning 2 chō (approximately 218 meters) each way and four caretakers assigned annually{{Sfn|Shinga Yamada Mausoleum (National History)|ja|磯長山田陵（国史）}}{{Sfn|Takamatsu Kofun (Heibonsha)|ja|高松古墳（平凡社）|1986}}. {{gallery |width=220 |lines=2 |File:Yamada Takatsuka kohun aerial.jpg|Aerial view of Yamada Takatsuka Kofun (1985) |File:Futagozuka Kofun (Taishi, Osaka), enkei from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun-2.jpg|View of Futagozuka Kofun from Yamada Takatsuka Kofun }} == notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/033/ Shinga Yamada Mausoleum] -
